findings.title: Other bindings from "bun:bundle" are dropped without being declared, so using them throws a ReferenceError at runtime.
findings.body: Only the `feature` specifier gets a declared symbol. The whole import is then replaced with `S.Empty`, and three kinds of binding are left without any declaration: other named specifiers, a default import (`import b from "bun:bundle"`), and a namespace import (`import * as b from "bun:bundle"`). Any use of them, such as `b.feature("X")`, compiles to a reference to an unbound global and throws `ReferenceError` at runtime. The warning on line 2683 says the name "will be undefined", which is not what happens. Default and star imports get no diagnostic at all. Fix: report an error for `stmt.default_name`, `stmt.star_name_loc` and unknown specifiers. If they really should evaluate to `undefined`, declare their refs and bind them to `undefined`.

findings.title: Feature flags are not part of the runtime transpiler cache key, so cached output can be stale.
findings.body:
`bundler_feature_flags` is added to `Runtime.Features`, but it is not in `hash_fields_for_runtime_transpiler`, and nothing else in the hash uses the flag set. `bun run` and `bun test` use the RuntimeTranspilerCache for large enough source files. So if you run `bun run --feature=X big.ts` and then `bun run big.ts`, the second run can load the cached output where `feature("X")` was already turned into `true`. That gives the wrong branch.

Fix: mix the sorted set of enabled flags into the cache hash, or turn the cache off when any flag is set. A file that imports `bun:bundle` could also skip the cache.

held.title: `feature()` results may be served stale from the runtime transpiler cache.
held.body: With `bun run --feature=X`, `feature()` is folded to `true` or `false` in the transpiled output. If the runtime transpiler cache key (the hashed `RuntimeFeatures` fields in runtime.zig, which I could not see) does not include the set of feature flags, a later run with different `--feature` flags reuses the old output. That cache is used for large files. The code inside the feature check then runs, or is skipped, against what the user asked for. Fix: add the enabled flag names to the runtime cache hash, or turn off the cache when `bun:bundle` is imported.

held.title: The transpiler keeps a pointer into the JS config's `features` set, which may not live as long as the bundle.
held.body: `transpiler.options.bundler_feature_flags = &config.features;` stores the address of a `StringSet` owned by the `Bun.build` config. If `config` here is a by-value copy, or the config is deinitialized (line 817 frees `self.features`) while parse tasks on worker threads still read `bundler_feature_flags`, those lookups read freed memory. I could not see whether `config` points into the long-lived completion task. Fix: confirm the pointer is stable for the whole bundle, or copy the set into the transpiler's allocator.

held.title: Freeing the shared flag set in BundleOptions.deinit can cause a double free or leave a dangling pointer.
held.body:
The `StringSet` is held only by pointer, and `BundleOptions` is copied by value in several places. For example, bundle_v2 builds extra client/SSR transpilers from the main transpiler's options, and each parse copies the pointer into `opts.features`. If more than one `Transpiler` that holds the same copied pointer gets deinit-ed, the set is freed twice. Also, any parse still running after the first deinit reads freed memory.

I could not see every place that copies or deinits these options, so this may not happen in practice. Fix: give the set one clear owner, such as the CLI context or the JSBundler config, or reset the pointer to the empty set after the copy is made.
